title: Homi Bhabha
desc: 1960s-inspired graphics for a documentary on Homi Bhabha.
lead: I created 1960s-inspired graphics and motion for Prachyam’s Who Killed Bhabha?
body: Prachyam’s film looks at Homi Bhabha’s contribution to Indian nuclear science and the circumstances of his death. I worked on the graphics and motion design, bringing archival images, documents and scientific references into the sequences shown here.
detail: I used typography, texture and compositing to connect the archival material. The 1960s-inspired treatment gave portraits, records and institutional scenes a consistent visual style.

story.challenge: Prachyam’s Who Killed Bhabha? looks at the scientist’s life and death. My brief was to give its archival photographs, documents and scientific references a consistent period treatment.
story.ownership: As Creative Lead and Art Director at Prachyam, I was the sole contributor to the work presented: archival composition, visual treatment and motion-design execution.
decisions: Use a 1960s-inspired graphic treatment to place the sequences in the period.
Connect material from different sources with consistent typography and texture.
Build sequences around portraits, institutions and records, including the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research.
story.result: The work became part of the documentary released on Prachyam OTT. This selection brings together my graphics and motion sequences for the film.
